re_verification_of_the_dispatch_statemen.result: UNCHANGED. Every namespace held the state the dispatch recorded.
re_verification_of_the_dispatch_statemen.additional_namespace_found: `cursor` (native Cursor tools, GenerateImage only). Not an MCP server and carries no namespaceStatus, which is why a status-oriented census can miss it.

how_needsauth_actually_behaves.finding: A namespace in needsAuth is not merely unauthenticated — its tools are not registered at all. GetDynamicTools returns an empty tools array, and an attempt to invoke a known tool name in that namespace fails at resolution rather than at authorisation.
how_needsauth_actually_behaves.response: Error: MCP server does not exist: Supabase. Use GetDynamicTools to discover available servers.
how_needsauth_actually_behaves.why_it_matters: There is no partial or degraded access to a needsAuth namespace, and no agent-side workaround. It is a hard boundary until a human authenticates. Any plan that routes through an unauthenticated namespace is not a plan.

namespaces.transport: Cursor-internal, authenticated by the run's own principal
namespaces.unlocks: Run identity and metadata; environment configuration and effective egress policy; the run's event log; the pending follow-up queue; enumeration of sibling and prior cloud agents; retrieval of another run's transcript, diff metadata, setup logs and environment info; environment build listing, log retrieval and draft build triggering; disk snapshotting; automation lookup by id.
namespaces.worth_to_this_operation: HIGH, and already load-bearing. This is the observation-and-retrieval half of multi-lane orchestration — the route by which a controller sees what its lanes did without a human relaying it. batch-fetch-details in particular is how one lane's produced evidence reaches an independent acceptor. It does not create runs, which is the gap the Cursor API key closes.
namespaces.founder_action_to_authenticate: None. Already authenticated as the run principal.
namespaces.caveat: Read and diagnostic only. It cannot create an agent run, so it cannot remove the founder from the dispatch path on its own.

namespaces.transport: Cursor-internal, authenticated by the run's own principal
namespaces.unlocks: Event-driven waiting instead of polling: terminal GitHub CI results on a branch, future GitHub pull request events, and timer-triggered follow-ups by cron or delay. Subscription listing and cancellation.
namespaces.worth_to_this_operation: HIGH for the coordination loop specifically. A lane that subscribes and ends its turn costs nothing while waiting, where a lane that polls burns budget and wall-clock. subscribe_timer also gives the programme a scheduler it does not otherwise have.
namespaces.founder_action_to_authenticate: None for GitHub CI, GitHub PR and timer subscriptions. Slack and Linear returns are documented in the bundled subscribe skill but require an account-level integration that is not present.
namespaces.authorise_now_or_later: N/A — active for the GitHub and timer surfaces
namespaces.caveat: This lane did not exercise a subscription. Its readiness is established by tool registration, not by a completed round trip. Labelled DOCUMENTED for behaviour, DIRECTLY_REPRODUCED for availability.

namespaces.transport: Remote MCP at mcp.supabase.com, OAuth to a Supabase account
namespaces.unlocks: Per the official tool list at https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/mcp.md: list_organizations, get_organization, list_projects, get_project, create_project, get_cost, get_project_url, get_publishable_keys, list_tables, list_extensions, list_migrations, apply_migration, execute_sql, get_advisors, list_edge_functions, get_edge_function, deploy_edge_function, list_branches, create_branch, list_storage_buckets, get_storage_config, search_docs.

worth_to_this_operation.general: MEDIUM-HIGH. The estate's own intelligence records Supabase migrations and functions in obzio-platform, Obzio-Control and Obzio-Luxury, and names an unresolved Supabase security boundary. get_advisors against those projects is a real security instrument, and execute_sql plus list_migrations would let a lane reconcile schema state without founder relay.
worth_to_this_operation.for_the_cursor_api_key_specifically: ZERO. This is the finding that matters. The published tool surface contains no tool that reads Edge Function secrets — the only occurrences of the word 'secret' in the documentation refer to OAuth client secrets for MCP client registration. Authenticating this namespace would not move the Cursor API key one step closer to being usable.

namespaces.founder_action_to_authenticate: In Cursor, open Customize in the sidebar, locate the Supabase MCP server, and complete the OAuth sign-in to the Supabase account that owns the Obzio projects. This can be done from the web at https://cursor.com/agents as well as from the desktop app: Cursor registers callbacks for both surfaces (https://www.cursor.com/agents/mcp/oauth/callback for web and Cursor Agents, http://localhost:8787/callback for desktop).
namespaces.authorise_now_or_later: LATER, and deliberately so. It is worth having, but it is not on the critical path of anything this programme is currently blocked on, and it must not be mistaken for the route to the Cursor API key.
namespaces.correction_to_the_dispatch_premise: The dispatch stated that MCP integrations are authenticated in the Cursor desktop IDE. The documentation shows two supported surfaces, web included, which makes this a lighter founder action than assumed.
